description: RRMPG is Frederik Kratzert and contributors' Python collection for experimenting with rainfall-runoff models. It provides Numba-based implementations and common simulation and calibration interfaces, including HBV and GR4J examples. Inputs are precipitation, evapotranspiration or temperature series, model parameters and initial stores; outputs are simulated discharge, optional storage trajectories and fitted parameters. Geographic coverage follows the catchment data. Public source is free under MIT, with API documentation and examples intended to make hydrological models inspectable and reusable. A limitation is that the project is described as work in progress, and model-specific time steps matter: the documented GR4J interface requires daily data. RRMPG can support catchment inflow and sensitivity simulations for reservoirs, drainage and water planning. Wflow (model-wflow) provides related distributed hydrological modelling context. This is a reusable model library, not a single course exercise. No catchment dataset was downloaded or calibration run.
